ask.headline: Approve the direction for vireo
ask.document:
# Direction: vireo

A landing page for a field recorder that names the bird singing at you.

Dials: DESIGN_VARIANCE 6 · MOTION_INTENSITY 3 · VISUAL_DENSITY 4.

**Mode: new build.** There is nothing to preserve, so the only constraint is
the subject, and the subject is unusually generous. This is a tool people use
outdoors, at dawn, holding a phone at arm's length, and the page has to make
somebody believe it will work before they have heard it work.

---

## 1. The subject, before the design

The product is a recorder that listens for eight seconds and prints a name.
The audience is not ornithologists. It is people who have a garden, a commute
past a hedge, or a dog that needs walking at six in the morning, and who have
started to notice that the noise has structure.

The page has one job: convince a person who is standing outside, right now,
that the eight seconds are worth it.

> A birdsong app that opens with a photograph of a bird has already lost. The
> whole promise is that you do not have to see it.

That sentence is the brief. Everything below serves it.

### 1.1 What the page must not be

Named specifically, because the category has a single default look and it is
already on four competitors:

- A phone mockup on a blurred green background.
- A grid of species cards with round photographs.
- A map with pins on it, and in particular:
  1. no clustering
  2. no heat overlay
  3. no radius picker
- The words `AI-powered` anywhere above the fold.

---

## 2. The hero is a spectrogram

The characteristic artefact of this subject is not a bird. It is a
**spectrogram**: the two dimensional plot of frequency against time that is
what the machine actually reads, and what a trained ear is doing without
knowing it.

The hero is one real spectrogram of one real recording, drawn full bleed,
animated left to right at the speed of the original audio, with the name
resolving underneath it at the moment the model resolves. Nothing else is on
the screen. No headline above it. The name is the headline.

The spectrogram is drawn from real data shipped as a small array, not as an
image, so it stays crisp at any width and can be redrawn per breakpoint.

### 2.1 The three recordings

Three, cycling, chosen because they look as different as they sound:

1. A song thrush, which repeats every phrase two or three times and therefore
   draws as a visibly periodic block.
   - The repeat is the tell, and it survives wind noise better than pitch.
   - Two or three is the range worth drawing.
2. A chiffchaff, two notes, which draws as a ladder.
3. A tawny owl, low and smooth, which draws as a single warm smear near the
   bottom of the frequency range and proves the plot is not decoration.

## 3. Colour

The palette comes from the spectrogram, not from a brand deck. A spectrogram
is conventionally plotted on a dark ground with intensity carried by a single
warm ramp, and that convention is a hundred years old and instantly legible.

| Token | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` | `#0C1116` | The ground. Cool, slightly blue, the colour of the plot canvas |
| `panel` | `#141B22` | Cards and the pricing table |
| `ink` | `#E8EEF2` | Primary text |
| `ink-2` | `#9AA7B1` | Secondary text and captions |
| `ramp-1` | `#2B4B6F` | Quietest audible band in the plot |
| `ramp-2` | `#C9772E` | Mid intensity |
| `ramp-3` | `#F2C14E` | The loudest band, and the only accent used in the interface |
| `rule` | `#1E262E` | Hairlines |
| `alt` | `#243040` | Used by `grep -o 'a\|b'` in the build script only |

`ramp-3` is the single accent. It appears on the primary control, on the
resolved name, and on the loudest band of the plot, which means the accent on
the page and the accent in the data are literally the same colour. That is the
whole colour idea and it is worth protecting.

### 3.1 What the ramp is not allowed to do

The three ramp values are for the plot. `ramp-2` never sets text, because it
sits at 4.1 to 1 on the ground and fails at body size. It is permitted as a
fill and as a one pixel rule and nowhere else.

---

## 4. Type

Two voices, and the split is functional rather than decorative.

| Role | Face | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Interface | Söhne, or Inter if the budget will not stretch | Neutral, and the page needs the plot to be the only thing with personality |
| Reading | Freight Text Pro | The species notes are genuinely editorial and run to four hundred words |
| Data | Söhne Mono | Frequencies, durations, confidence values |

Scale runs 13 / 15 / 17 / 22 / 34 / 56, and the 56 appears exactly once, on
the resolved name under the hero plot.

No uppercase. No tracking above `0.01em`. The subject is a soft continuous
signal and wide letterspaced capitals fight it.

## 5. Motion

`MOTION_INTENSITY` is 3, which means one orchestrated moment and nothing else.

The moment is the hero: the playhead crosses the spectrogram at real speed,
the plot fills behind it, and at 6.2 seconds the name fades up. It runs once
on load, then on demand from a single replay control.

Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the plot draws complete and the name is already
there. The information is identical; only the theatre is gone.

```
playhead:  transform translateX, 8000ms linear
name:      opacity 0 to 1, 400ms, starting at 6200ms
replay:    press scale 0.98, 90ms
```

Nothing else on the page moves. No scroll triggered reveals, no counters, no
parallax.

## 6. Layout

Content caps at 1180px. The hero is full bleed and is the only full bleed
element.

Below the hero the page is a single column at 680px, because the species notes
are the second most important thing and a two column marketing grid would
shred them. Three sections, in this order:

1. What it does, in one paragraph and one more spectrogram.
2. The notes, which are real writing about real species and are the reason
   anybody would send the page to somebody else.
3. Price, as a table, with no toggle and no crossed out anchor number.

---

## 7. Open questions for the build

1. The eight second recordings are roughly 40KB each as raw arrays. Three of
   them is 120KB of blocking data before the hero can draw. Worth it, or draw
   the first from an inline array and fetch the other two?
2. The tawny owl recording is genuinely low frequency and may be inaudible on
   a phone speaker. Keep it for the drawing and accept that, or drop to two?

Read the [spectrogram conventions note](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrogram)
before building section 2.

history.quote: The hero is a photograph. Section 2 of the direction says the hero is the spectrogram, and the reason it says so is the whole product argument.

history.text: you sent 4 of 9 back to the builder

findings.text: The resolved species name is set in `ramp-2` at 17px, which is 4.1 to 1 on the ground. Section 3.1 of the approved direction says in as many words that `ramp-2` never sets text.

The hero playhead animates `left` rather than `transform`, which is a layout pass on every frame of an eight second animation. On a mid range phone the whole hero drops below thirty frames a second, which is visible on the one element the page is built around.
No focus ring on the replay control. It is a real button, it is in the tab order, and it is invisible when it has focus.
The pricing table has a monthly and yearly toggle. The direction says no toggle, and the reason it says so is that the page has one price.
Species notes are capped at 52ch, which puts the four hundred word thrush note at nineteen lines of ragged column. The reading measure was the argument for the single column layout.
Three of the eight section headings are sentence case and five are title case.
The chiffchaff spectrogram is drawn at 240 samples where the other two are at 256, so its ladder sits two pixels lower than the others when they cycle.
`aria-label` on the replay control reads `replay button`. The role is already announced, so it says button twice.
